name: Reel
text: Standardize a single "ready-for-transcription" tag across all teams. This cuts confusion by replacing ad-hoc signals with one clear rule: only videos with that tag get transcribed. The trade-off is slower initial tagging, but it speeds up the whole pipeline by eliminating rework and miscommunication.

name: Scriv
text: The risk isn’t slower tagging—it’s that teams will game the system by slapping the tag on anything to hit volume targets, turning the "quality flag" into a rubber stamp. Better alternative: enforce a two-step gate—tagging *and* a 30-second spot-check by a dedicated reviewer before transcription starts. Settle it with a 1-week pilot: measure how often the check catches mislabeled videos versus the current ad-hoc chaos.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt the two-step gate: tagging plus a 30-second spot-check by a dedicated reviewer before transcription. This keeps the "ready" flag meaningful and prevents teams from gaming the system, which would flood the pipeline with low-quality transcripts and slow down the whole process. The trade-off is a small delay in the first step, but it guarantees higher-quality inputs and prevents rework downstream.

name: Sift
text: The real risk isn’t gaming the system—it’s that a dedicated reviewer becomes a bottleneck when volume spikes, turning the 30-second spot-check into a 5-minute delay. Instead, automate the gate: flag videos with the "ready" tag, then run a lightweight quality check (e.g., audio clarity score, minimum duration) before transcription. Settle it by testing both approaches—measure throughput and error rates over a week.
